statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if there exists a binary expression tree with the following properties: (1) it has exactly 4 leaves, labeled by the four elements of cards in some order, each used exactly once; (2) each internal node is labeled by one of '+', '-', '*', '/'; (3) every internal node has exactly two children (so the tree is a full binary tree with 3 internal nodes); (4) the tree is evaluated using real arithmetic, where for '/' the divisor must be non-zero; (5) the evaluated value is exactly 24. Equivalently, the four numbers can be combined using the allowed operations and parentheses to yield 24, using each number exactly once.
preconditions: cards is a slice of length 4, and for every index i with 0 <= i < 4, 1 <= cards[i] <= 9.

statement: The function returns the same result on both inputs: judge_point24(cards1) = judge_point24(cards2).
preconditions: cards1 and cards2 are two slices of length 4, and for every index i with 0 <= i < 4, 1 <= cards1[i] <= 9 and 1 <= cards2[i] <= 9. The multiset of elements of cards1 equals the multiset of elements of cards2 (i.e., cards2 is a permutation of cards1).
cards is a slice of length 4 equal to [1,1,1,1].
cards is a slice of length 4 equal to [4,1,8,7].
